question: Why does a conversation scene suddenly feel wrong if the camera jumps to the other side of the two actors?
answer: Because left and right swap. Film crews draw an imaginary line between the actors and keep the camera on one side, the 180-degree rule. Cross it and the woman who looked right now looks left, so viewers sense she has turned away. Directors break the rule on purpose when they want unease.
move: Your sense of where things are depends on where you are watching from.
ask: In an argument I had recently, how would it look from the other side of the table?
source: Katz, Film Directing Shot by Shot
reference: Steven D. Katz, Film Directing Shot by Shot: Visualizing from Concept to Screen, Michael Wiese Productions, 1991
